ingredients.name: Tuna (yellowfin or skipjack)
ingredients.notes: or any firm fish that won't break apart when stir-fried; cut into 3cm cubes

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: for the marinade, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Flour
ingredients.notes: for coating before frying; can mix with a little cornflour for extra crispness

ingredients.name: Oil for frying
ingredients.notes: for deep or shallow frying the fish cubes

ingredients.name: Chilli flakes
ingredients.notes: for the sauce, in addition to the marinade chilli powder

ingredients.name: Chilli sauce
ingredients.notes: optional; adds extra heat and tang on top of the ketchup

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.notes: do not use dark soy sauce, as it dulls the dish's signature red colour

ingredients.name: Banana peppers or green bell pepper

steps.instruction: Cut the fish into 3cm cubes. Marinate with turmeric, chilli powder, salt, and lime juice for about 15-30 minutes.

Toss the marinated fish lightly in the flour, shaking off any excess. Heat the oil and deep-fry or shallow-fry the fish cubes until golden and just cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Avoid overcooking, as the fish will cook again briefly in the sauce. Drain on paper towels and set aside.
In a separate wok or pan, heat a little oil. Add the cinnamon stick, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves, and sauté until the garlic starts to turn golden at the edges, about 1 minute.
Add the chilli flakes and stir briefly over low heat until they darken slightly, taking care not to burn them.
Add the ketchup, chilli sauce (if using), soy sauce, sugar, and water. Mix well and let the sauce heat through and come to a gentle simmer.
Add the onion and banana peppers (or bell pepper). Stir-fry briefly, about 1 minute, keeping the vegetables crunchy.

Add the fried fish cubes and tomato wedges. Gently toss everything together over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, until the fish is well coated in the glossy sauce -- handle gently to avoid breaking up the fish pieces.
Taste and adjust the seasoning -- more ketchup for sweetness, more chilli for heat, salt as needed. Serve hot with rice, bread, or naan.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, joyofeatingtheworld.com, and pulse.lk for technique and sauce-balance consistency
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 5+ independent sources; strong agreement on tuna/firm fish as the preferred protein and the same red-sauce technique as devilled chicken
notes: Tuna or another firm-fleshed fish (such as sailfish, locally called thalapath) is strongly preferred for this dish, since it holds together through two cooking stages -- first frying, then stir-frying in the sauce -- without flaking apart. Like devilled chicken (sl_032), this is a Sri Lankan-Chinese fusion dish, sharing the same core red-sauce technique built from ketchup, chilli, and soy sauce. Skin-on fish pieces can help further with structural integrity if available. A coconut-milk variant exists for those who want extra gravy, but the dry, sauce-coated version presented here is the more iconic restaurant and home-cooking style.
